short: An English Catholic conspirator whose failed attempt to assassinate James I during the Gunpowder Plot is commemorated annually in Britain.
full:
Guy Fawkes was a devout English Catholic and a military veteran who became the most famous conspirator in the 1605 Gunpowder Plot. Having left England to fight for the Spanish in the Eighty Years' War, he gained considerable expertise in explosives. Fawkes was recruited by Robert Catesby to join a conspiracy aiming to assassinate the Protestant King James I and the entire English political establishment by blowing up the House of Lords during the State Opening of Parliament.

The plot was discovered after an anonymous warning letter was sent to a Catholic noble. In the early hours of 5 November 1605, authorities searched the cellars beneath Parliament and discovered Fawkes guarding thirty-six barrels of gunpowder. Despite enduring severe torture at the Tower of London, he initially refused to reveal his co-conspirators. Fawkes was sentenced to be hanged, drawn, and quartered, though he evaded the worst of the execution by jumping from the scaffold and breaking his neck. His failure is still commemorated every 5 November as Guy Fawkes Night.
